docs.purpose: Where the payment provider sends the user if they back out of paying. It is a single reassuring message: no charge was made, and to try again they should return to the mobile app and tap the subscribe link. It fetches nothing and changes nothing.
docs.data_story: This surface reaches **no API contract at all** — every value it shows is local, passed in as a prop, or read from the device.
docs.under_126: **RE-PROJECT** — it writes nothing and holds no Layer-3 store, so the move is short — the server already assembles the payload and only the rendering is client-side. It renders through the STATIC renderer (content source and SEO, or a declared redirect alone), reading no contract. It owns no component of its own, so its `owns.components[]` is an empty array — a legal answer, written down.

contracts: none — no /api/ string and no fetch in src/app/subscribe/cancel/page.tsx
tables: none — no SQL, no db client import
emits: none — no captureEvent import in src/app/subscribe/cancel/page.tsx

versioning.why: Twenty-two lines of static copy that nothing consumes and nothing parses.

inputs.why: No fetch, no props, no search params — it is a server component with no interactivity at all, by the file's own design note and by the absence of any 'use client' directive.

outputs.why: The user backed out on the Stripe-hosted page: no charge was made and no state changed anywhere, here or server-side.

state.why: No hook of any kind — it is a plain server component returning one tree.

staleness.why: The copy changes only on redeploy; there is no server value on the page.

session.why: /subscribe/cancel is in PUBLIC_PATHS as a Stripe redirect target for a sessionless visitor, and the lock pins it public.

checks.why: Purely descriptive and deliberately so: the page's whole contract is that abandoning checkout changes nothing, so the assertion worth keeping is that no row of any kind appears — there is no threshold to bound.
Stripe redirects here without a session; if the fail-closed default ever reclaims this path the visitor is bounced to /login from a payment flow they just abandoned.

errors.why: No fetch and no branch — no failure is reachable.

emits.why: Nothing is emitted, so an abandoned checkout leaves no trace on the web side at all.

offers.why: No placement — the page has no inventory and no slot.

limitations.what: The page names a product that is being renamed.
limitations.measured: src/app/subscribe/cancel/page.tsx:16-17 says "return to the Buildo app"; src/app/layout.tsx:6 and src/app/login/page.tsx:34 both say MaxBLD (Spec 117).

notes: Server component, no interactivity, single unconditional render - hence states=['static'] rather than an empty array. Copy still says 'the Buildo app', pre-dating the Spec 117 MaxBLD rename. MEASURED 2026-09-15: the only web-product page with no 'use client' directive — a genuine server component (the file says so at :5 and the absence of the directive confirms it). a11y.labels is `none` rather than `complete` because the page has no interactive element and no label; touch_target_min_px stays UNRESEARCHED for the same reason the other rows do — the vocabulary has no value for "no interactive target".

measured_gate.why: classifyRoute('/subscribe/cancel') matches the PUBLIC_PATHS exact entry '/subscribe/cancel' -> 'public'; every earlier arm (files, /_next/, /api/auth/, exact-public-API, /api/admin/, /admin, authenticated APIs, PUBLIC_PREFIXES) fails to match.

programme.why: The subscription and Stripe hand-off, which resolves an entitlement per PRODUCT — so it serves both and belongs to neither.
